To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cAMP receptor (CRP) protein of Eschericia coli can be cross-linked by a bifunctional reagant (oPDM), the nature of the cross-link is dependent on the conformation of CRP, and the cross-linked protein is protease-sensitive.
o-phenyldimaleimide, a bifunctional reagant, cross-links the two subunits within the protomer of the cyclic adenosine 5'-monophosphatase receptor protein of Escheirichia coli.
oPDM reacts with two cysteine residues on the CRP protomer, one on each of its two subunits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of activation of the cyclic AMP receptor protein (CR) of Eschericia coli by cyclic AMP (cAMP).
the study of conformational changes in the cAMP (3',5'-cyclic adenosinemonophosphate) receptor of E. coli, the CRP (cAMP receptor protein).
the conformational changes that occur in the cAMP receptor of Escherichi coli upon binding the effector molecule, cAMP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conformation of the CRP subunits in the cAMP-bound and unbound forms of CRP is different.
oPDM cross-links CRP subunits in a manner which depends upon the conformational states of CRP, and that the conformational changes induced by cAMP result in a more accessible target for the reagent.
the cross-linking is a consequence of cAMP binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cAMP receptor site is in the cAMP-bound conformation of the protein.
the conformation of the CRP subunits is different when cAMP is bound.
the conformation of CRP is dependent upon the presence of c-AMP and that the conformational changes induced by cAMP are not readily reversible.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of c-AMP induces a conformational change in the CRP protein that makes it more susceptible to proteolytic cleavage and that o-phenylyenemalide can be used as a probe to study this conformational change.
oPDM cross-links the subunits of CRP in a conformation-dependent manner, with the rate of crosslinking increasing upon binding cAMP.
CRP is a protein that is highly susceptible to cross-linking, which makes it an excellent candidate for the use of cross-linking agents in the study of protein interactions.
